# Control narrative template for pump and on/off valve equipment modules

## 1. How the template stops drift

| Rule | Effect |
|---|---|
| Write behavior once, in a class narrative (common base EM, PMP, VLV). | One text for about 120 pumps and 300 valves. |
| An instance sheet holds data and deltas only: tags, options, setpoint values, instance interlock rows, instance alarm bindings, open items. | Nothing is copied, so nothing drifts. |
| An instance sheet never restates a class requirement. It may override a class parameter or add its own FR-<tag>-NNN. | A deviation is visible as an ID. |
| Class revision is tied to the PLC library version. A class change goes through MOC. A query on the instance register's class column lists the affected tags. | Change impact is a query, not a document search. |
| Class requirements are type-tested once per library version. Instance FAT tests only the bindings, the values and the I/O. | FAT effort scales with the deltas. |
| Generate the instance sheet from the tag database where possible. Write prose only for deviations. | Most instances need no paragraph at all. |

Class requirement IDs are FR-EM-NNN (common), FR-PMP-NNN and FR-VLV-NNN. Test codes: **T1** is the library type test, done once per library version. **T2** is the instance FAT check.

## 2. Common base: FR-EM (all pumps and valves)

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-EM-001 | The module has the modes Out of Service, Manual and Auto. The operator selects the mode. The module accepts Out of Service only when the equipment is at rest or FAULTED. | T1: select each mode in each state |
| FR-EM-002 | The module accepts commands only from the source of the active mode: operator in Manual, parent in Auto. It ignores and logs all other commands. | T1: send from both sources in both modes |
| FR-EM-003 | In Out of Service, the outputs go to the fail position. The module rejects all commands, suppresses its alarms and reports "unavailable" to the parent. | T1 |
| FR-EM-004 | A latched fault stays until the operator sends Reset and all causes are clear. Reset does not start or move the equipment. | T1 |
| FR-EM-005 | A signal with bad quality is treated as its protective state. Each class defines that state. | T1: force bad quality per signal |
| FR-EM-006 | After a PLC restart, the outputs go to the fail position. The module keeps its mode and its latched faults. It does not restart or reopen on its own. | T1: power-cycle test |
| FR-EM-007 | The module logs each state change, command and fault with time and source. | T1 |
| FR-EM-008 | The faceplate shows mode, state, first-out fault and unmet permissives. A rejected command shows the first unmet permissive. Operator commands need operator access. Parameter changes need engineer access. | T1 |

## 3. Pump class (PMP)

### 3.1 Purpose and options

The module controls one motor-driven pump. It interfaces with the parent module (commands and status), the starter or drive, and the instance interlocks.

| Option | Adds | Instance supplies |
|---|---|---|
| OPT-VFD | Speed reference, drive ready, drive comms | Min and max speed |
| OPT-SUCT | Dry-run protection on a suction pressure transmitter | PT tag, three pressure values, trip delay |

Signals are named `<tag>.<signal>`. The signals are RUN_CMD, RUN_FB, DRV_FAULT, DRV_READY, COMM_OK, SPEED_REF and SPEED_FB.

### 3.2 States (ISA-106)

| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | RUN_FB false, no latched fault | STARTING, FAULTED | Operator (Manual) or parent (Auto) | Manual / automatic |
| STARTING | Start accepted (FR-PMP-001) | RUNNING, STOPPING, FAULTED | Module | Automatic |
| RUNNING | RUN_FB true for the run-confirm time | STOPPING, FAULTED | Module | Automatic |
| STOPPING | Stop accepted | STOPPED, FAULTED | Operator, parent or module | Manual / automatic |
| FAULTED | Any trip (section 3.5) | STOPPED | Operator Reset | Manual |

### 3.3 Sequences

| Seq | Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Start | S1 | Check permissives. With OPT-VFD, write the clamped speed reference. | All permissives true | One scan | Reject command. Show first unmet permissive. |
| Start | S2 | Set RUN_CMD. | RUN_FB true | SP-PMP-01 | FAULTED (START FAIL). Remove RUN_CMD. |
| Start | S3 | Hold RUN_CMD. | RUN_FB true without break | SP-PMP-02 | FAULTED (START FAIL). Remove RUN_CMD. |
| Stop | P1 | Remove RUN_CMD. | RUN_FB false | SP-PMP-03 | FAULTED (STOP FAIL). Keep RUN_CMD off. |

### 3.4 Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-PMP-001 | The module accepts Start only in STOPPED, with no latched fault, all permissives true, and the minimum stopped time (SP-PMP-05) elapsed. | T1 |
| FR-PMP-002 | The module runs the Start sequence of 3.3. | T1: normal start, then each timeout |
| FR-PMP-003 | The module runs the Stop sequence of 3.3. It accepts Stop in STARTING and RUNNING. | T1 |
| FR-PMP-004 | On any trip in 3.5, the module removes RUN_CMD at once, goes to FAULTED, and stores the first-out cause. | T1: inject each cause |
| FR-PMP-005 | If RUN_FB goes false in RUNNING without a Stop, the module trips (UNEXPECTED STOP). | T1 |
| FR-PMP-006 | If RUN_FB is true in STOPPED, the module removes RUN_CMD and trips (RUN WITHOUT COMMAND). | T1 |
| FR-PMP-007 | If COMM_OK is false for the comm-loss time (SP-PMP-04), the module trips (COMM FAIL). The drive is set to stop on comms loss. | T1; T2: pull drive comms cable |
| FR-PMP-008 | Fail position is stopped. All outputs de-energize to stop. | T1 |
| FR-PMP-030 | With OPT-SUCT, the suction pressure above the start permissive value is a start permissive. | T1, T2 |
| FR-PMP-031 | With OPT-SUCT, if pressure stays below the low-low trip value for the trip delay in STARTING or RUNNING, the module trips (DRY RUN). | T1, T2 |
| FR-PMP-032 | Bad quality of the suction PT counts as pressure below the low-low trip value. The same trip delay applies. | T1, T2: wire-break |
| FR-PMP-033 | A DRY RUN trip is latched. Reset needs pressure above the start permissive value and an operator Reset. | T1, T2 |
| FR-PMP-034 | Pressure below the low warning value in RUNNING raises LOW SUCTION. The pump keeps running. | T1 |
| FR-PMP-035 | DRY RUN is BPCS equipment protection, not a safety instrumented function. If a hazard study requires an SIS function, the SRS holds it. | Review |
| FR-PMP-040 | With OPT-VFD, the module clamps SPEED_REF between the minimum and maximum speed. | T1, T2 |
| FR-PMP-041 | In Manual, SPEED_REF is the operator speed setpoint. In Auto, it is the parent speed setpoint. The drive ramps limit the rate of change. | T1 |
| FR-PMP-042 | With OPT-VFD, DRV_READY is a start permissive. DRV_FAULT is a trip. | T1 |

### 3.5 Interlocks (class rows)

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| DRV_FAULT true | Trip, coast stop | Latched | Clear cause, Reset |
| START FAIL, STOP FAIL | Trip | Latched | Reset |
| FR-PMP-005, -006, -007 conditions | Trip | Latched | Clear cause, Reset |
| DRY RUN (OPT-SUCT) | Trip | Latched | FR-PMP-033 |
| Instance interlock | Per instance sheet | Per instance sheet | Per instance sheet |

The hardwired E-stop is outside this module. It is covered by the electrical design and, where applicable, the SRS.

### 3.6 Regulatory control

The module has no PID loop. Its output is SPEED_REF (FR-PMP-040, -041). Any flow or pressure loop is in the parent narrative. The parent must write SPEED_REF only to this module.

### 3.7 Alarms

Priorities are provisional until the plant alarm philosophy is confirmed.

| Alarm | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| DRIVE FAULT | DRV_FAULT | Medium | Read the drive display. Fix the cause. Reset. |
| START FAIL | S2 or S3 timeout | Medium | Check the drive and the motor. Reset. |
| STOP FAIL | P1 timeout | Medium | Isolate power at the drive. Call maintenance. |
| UNEXPECTED STOP | FR-PMP-005 | Medium | Check the drive and the process. Reset. |
| RUN WITHOUT COMMAND | FR-PMP-006 | High | Check the drive for a stuck run. Call maintenance. |
| COMM FAIL | FR-PMP-007 | Medium | Check the network cable and the drive. Reset. |
| DRY RUN TRIP | FR-PMP-031 | High | Make sure the source has liquid. Open the suction valves. Reset. |
| LOW SUCTION | FR-PMP-034 | Low | Check the source level and the suction valves. |
| SUCTION PT BAD | PT quality bad | Medium | Check the transmitter and its wiring. |

### 3.8 Abnormal handling

| Event | Response |
|---|---|
| Bad PV | FR-EM-005, FR-PMP-032 |
| Comms loss | FR-PMP-007 |
| PLC power loss and restart | FR-EM-006. State starts as STOPPED. |
| Drive power loss while running | FR-PMP-005 |
| Fail position | FR-PMP-008 |

### 3.9 Class setpoint defaults

| ID | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-PMP-01 | 10 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-02 | 2 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-03 | 30 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-04 | 2 | s | confirm |
| SP-PMP-05 | 10 | s | confirm |

Meanings: 01 start-feedback timeout, 02 run-confirm time, 03 stop-feedback timeout, 04 comm-loss time, 05 minimum stopped time.

## 4. On/off valve class (VLV)

### 4.1 Parameters (set per instance)

| Parameter | Allowed values |
|---|---|
| Fail position | Open, Closed |
| Actuation | Single solenoid, double solenoid |
| Feedback | Open limit and closed limit |

### 4.2 States

| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLOSED | Closed limit true, open limit false | OPENING, FAULTED | Operator (Manual) or parent (Auto) | Manual / automatic |
| OPENING | Open accepted (FR-VLV-002) | OPEN, CLOSING, FAULTED | Module | Automatic |
| OPEN | Open limit true, closed limit false | CLOSING, FAULTED | Module | Automatic |
| CLOSING | Close accepted | CLOSED, OPENING, FAULTED | Operator, parent or module | Manual / automatic |
| FAULTED | Fault in 4.5 | CLOSED or OPEN (from feedback, on Reset) | Operator Reset | Manual |

### 4.3 Sequences

| Seq | Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open | V1 | Check permissives. | All true | One scan | Reject command. Show first unmet permissive. |
| Open | V2 | Command the open output. | Open limit true, closed limit false | SP-VLV-01 | FAULTED (TRAVEL FAIL). Hold outputs. |
| Close | V3 | Check permissives. | All true | One scan | Reject command. Show first unmet permissive. |
| Close | V4 | Command the close output. | Closed limit true, open limit false | SP-VLV-02 | FAULTED (TRAVEL FAIL). Hold outputs. |

### 4.4 Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-VLV-001 | The module sets output logic from the three parameters in 4.1. | T1: one test per parameter combination |
| FR-VLV-002 | The module accepts Open only in CLOSED or CLOSING, with all permissives true. It accepts Close only in OPEN or OPENING, with all permissives true. | T1 |
| FR-VLV-003 | The module runs the sequences of 4.3. | T1: normal travel, then each timeout |
| FR-VLV-004 | If both limits are true, or both are false at rest, for the position-fault delay (SP-VLV-03), the module goes to FAULTED (POSITION INVALID). | T1 |
| FR-VLV-005 | If the limit for the commanded position is lost with no command for SP-VLV-03, the module goes to FAULTED (POSITION LOST). | T1 |
| FR-VLV-006 | On Reset, the module takes its state from the limits if they are valid. Otherwise it stays FAULTED. | T1 |
| FR-VLV-007 | Fail position is the parameter in 4.1. All outputs de-energize to the fail position. | T1 |
| FR-VLV-008 | An instance interlock can force a position. The force overrides all commands in Manual and Auto. It resets automatically unless the instance row says latched. | T1, T2 |
| FR-VLV-009 | Bad quality on a limit signal counts as limit not made (FR-EM-005). | T1 |

### 4.5 Alarms, abnormal handling and defaults

| Alarm | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| TRAVEL FAIL | Timeout in 4.3 | Medium | Check air supply, solenoid and limits. Reset. |
| POSITION INVALID | FR-VLV-004 | Medium | Check limit switches and wiring. Reset. |
| POSITION LOST | FR-VLV-005 | Medium | Check air supply and the actuator. Reset. |

| Event | Response |
|---|---|
| Bad PV | FR-VLV-009 |
| Air or power loss | Valve moves to fail position. Module follows FR-VLV-005. |
| PLC restart | FR-EM-006, FR-VLV-007 |
| Comms loss to remote I/O | Limit signals go bad. FR-VLV-009 applies. |

| ID | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-VLV-01 | 5 | s | confirm |
| SP-VLV-02 | 5 | s | confirm |
| SP-VLV-03 | 1 | s | confirm |

Meanings: 01 open travel timeout, 02 close travel timeout, 03 position-fault delay. Mixproof (seat-lift) valves are not covered (OI-8).

## 5. Instance sheet template

| Section | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Header | Tag, class, class revision, library version, area, parent module | Instance register |
| Options | Option list and parameters | Instance register |
| Tags | Tags this module uses (no instrument index was given) | Tag database |
| Setpoints | Overrides of class defaults, plus option values | Instance register |
| Interlocks | Instance cause | effect | latched | reset rows | Written per instance |
| Alarms | Alarm text bound to tags and priority overrides | Alarm database |
| Deviations | Overrides of class FRs as FR-<tag>-NNN | Written per instance |
| FAT checklist | Instance tests, each tied to a class FR | Generated |
| Open items | Item, owner, due date | Written per instance |

Sections 1, 3, 5 and 9 of the standard narrative (purpose, states, sequences, operator interface) come from the class. The instance does not restate them.

## 6. Worked example: P-4021 instance sheet

**Header.** Tag P-4021, CIP supply pump. Class PMP, revision and library version to be taken from the register. Options OPT-VFD and OPT-SUCT. Area CIP. Parent: CIP supply module (tag open, OI-4).

**Tags.** P-4021 (motor), VFD-4021 (drive tag assumed, OI-5), PT-4022 (suction pressure, location assumed, OI-1).

**Setpoints (overrides and option values).**

| ID | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-4021-01 | 30 | kPa(g) | confirm |
| SP-4021-02 | 15 | kPa(g) | confirm |
| SP-4021-03 | 3 | s | confirm |
| SP-4021-04 | 22 | kPa(g) | confirm |
| SP-4021-05 | 30 | % | confirm |
| SP-4021-06 | 100 | % | confirm |
| SP-4021-07 | 60 | % | confirm |
| SP-4021-08 | 10 | s | confirm |
| SP-4021-09 | 10 | s | confirm |

Meanings: 01 suction start permissive (FR-PMP-030, -033), 02 low-low trip (FR-PMP-031), 03 trip delay (FR-PMP-031), 04 low warning (FR-PMP-034), 05 minimum speed, 06 maximum speed (FR-PMP-040), 07 default manual speed, 08 drive acceleration ramp, 09 drive deceleration ramp. The ramps are drive parameters. No class default is overridden.

**Regulatory control.** SPEED_REF follows FR-PMP-041. No local loop exists.

**Instance interlock row.**

| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-4022 below SP-4021-02 for SP-4021-03, or PT-4022 bad | P-4021 trips (DRY RUN), coast stop | Latched | PT-4022 above SP-4021-01, then operator Reset |

No other instance interlock is confirmed (OI-3).

**Alarm bindings.** Class responses in 3.7 apply.

| Alarm text | Class alarm | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| P-4021 DRY RUN TRIP | DRY RUN TRIP | High |
| P-4021 LOW SUCTION | LOW SUCTION | Low |
| PT-4022 BAD | SUCTION PT BAD | Medium |

**Deviations.** None. No FR-P4021-NNN exists.

**Instance FAT checklist.**

| ID | Test | Class FR |
|---|---|---|
| IT-4021-01 | Simulate PT-4022 at both range ends. Check scaling. | FR-PMP-030 |
| IT-4021-02 | Set PT-4022 below SP-4021-01. Send Start. Check the rejection and the first unmet permissive. | FR-PMP-030 |
| IT-4021-03 | Run the pump. Drop PT-4022 below SP-4021-02 for less than SP-4021-03. Check no trip. | FR-PMP-031 |
| IT-4021-04 | Repeat for longer than SP-4021-03. Check trip, coast stop, latched state and alarm. | FR-PMP-031 |
| IT-4021-05 | Restore PT-4022 above SP-4021-01. Check the trip stays until Reset. | FR-PMP-033 |
| IT-4021-06 | Break the PT-4022 wire while running. Check the trip after SP-4021-03. | FR-PMP-032 |
| IT-4021-07 | Command speed below SP-4021-05 and above SP-4021-06. Check the clamp. | FR-PMP-040 |
| IT-4021-08 | Pull the drive comms cable while running. Check the trip. | FR-PMP-007 |
| IT-4021-09 | Compare the PLC parameter values with the setpoint list. | Parameter match |

**Open items.**

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | Confirm PT-4022 is on the pump suction. Confirm its range and units. | Process engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-2 | Confirm the provisional pressure setpoints against the pump curve and NPSH. | Process engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-3 | Decide whether a discharge-valve permissive or other instance interlock is needed. | Process engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-4 | Give the parent module tag. Define how it sets the speed (open-loop or flow/pressure loop). | Controls lead | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-5 | Confirm the drive tag and the drive stop-on-comms-loss parameter. | Integrator | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-6 | Confirm that DRY RUN is BPCS equipment protection and needs no SIS function. | Controls lead | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-7 | Operations sign-off of states, prompts and alarm priorities (class and instance). | Operations lead | 2026-11-27 |
| OI-8 | Decide the scope of mixproof (seat-lift) valves. Add a class option if needed. | Controls lead | 2026-11-20 |

The dates are proposals. Confirm them with the owners.

## 7. Check against the pre-presentation list

- No setpoint or trip value appears in prose. All values are in the lists in 3.9, 4.5 and 6.
- Every requirement has an ID and a test method. Class FRs are tested once (T1). Instance bindings are tested through IT-4021-NN.
- Every state has an entry condition and exits. Every sequence step has a timeout and a failure response.
- Bad PV, comms loss, power loss and restart, and fail positions are defined in FR-EM-005 and -006, 3.8 and 4.5.
- Interlocks and alarms are written out in the reply, because no chart or database was given.
- The SIS function is referenced to the SRS (FR-PMP-035).
- STE editing pass: apply it to the final text after operations sign-off of the wording. The state names and prompts are the items they must approve.
